jordan (customer): Hey -- our rerank results look wrong since we bumped to the TS SDK v1.4.2. Scores are coming back as a mix of "0" strings and weird negative floats. We pass 5 candidates and expect a descending rank by score but ordering is all over the place. Blocker for search relevance. Example payload we send (TS client):
```json
{
  "query": "how to reset password",
  "candidates": ["a","b","c","d","e"],
  "max_results": 5
}
```
And response (snippet):
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"candidate": "b", "score": "0"},
    {"candidate": "a", "score": -3.14159},
    {"candidate": "c", "score": "0.823"}
  ]
}
```
I also tried curl against the API and got proper numeric floats. Using the TS SDK seems to be producing/serializing something weird. Can someone investigate?

maya: Thanks Jordan — can you paste the exact SDK call and the package version? Also did you upgrade both the server/api and the client at the same time? Any error codes in our logs?

jordan (customer): SDK call looks like:
```ts
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.rerank({
  model: 'r-ada-rerank',
  input: query,
  candidates: candidatesArray,
  top_k: 5
});
```
Version: 1.4.2. Server is hosted (hosted API) — we didn't touch server. No 4xx/5xx from the client, just semantically wrong scores.

sam: @maya assigning to SDK. I can repro locally, thanks for the minimal example. When I log the outgoing request from the TS client I see the body includes scores as strings in the rerank request marshal step (we shouldn't be sending scores on request normally but some callers attach initial scores; the serialization path is buggy). Quick repro: the helper `attachScores` uses `map(String)` in one code path.###### gist:```ts
// bug: converting numbers to strings unintentionally
candidates = candidates.map(c => ({ ...c, score: String(c.score) }));
```
That explains the server seeing strings and then our normalization logic does `parseFloat(score)` and treats empty/invalid as NaN which flows into softmax and yields extreme negative numbers. I'll open a PR.

eli: I pulled the server logs for request 1769892345 (customer request id). Server parser shows: `WARN rerank: score parseFloat -> NaN for candidate id=...`, then later: `WARN rerank: numeric overflow during softmax, result set clipped` — so that exactly matches the symptom. We currently have a permissive parser that expects numbers but tolerates strings; but downstream math paths don't guard against NaN.

sam: Fix plan: 1) Change TS SDK serialization to avoid forcing scores to strings (remove the `String()` coercion). 2) Add a defensive server-side guard: treat non-numeric scores as missing (fall back to uniform scoring) and log a better structured error. 3) Add regression test to TS SDK for candidate serialization and to server tests for NaN handling.

ci-bot: Deploy check triggered for sdk PR #1234 by sam — tests: unit 178 passed, integration 42/45 failing (flaky network mocks).

maya: @sam please also include a minor version bump and mention in changelog that v1.4.3 fixes rerank serialization bug. Jordan, would you be willing to validate a pre-release? We can cut a release candidate and DM you the tarball.

jordan (customer): Yes please, we'd test the RC. Also FYI we saw an intermittent 401 earlier when keys rotated but that was separate — fixed after reloading key. This issue is specifically with ranking quality.

sam: created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1234 — patch removes coercion and adds test. Example change:```diff
- candidates = candidates.map(c => ({ ...c, score: String(c.score) }));
+ candidates = candidates.map(c => ({ ...c, score: typeof c.score === 'number' ? c.score : undefined }));
```
I'll ship v1.4.3 once CI is green.

eli: backend mitigation in flight: will update parser to `const s = parseFloat(raw); if (Number.isNaN(s)) { log.debug("rerank: bad score, treating as missing"); s = null; }` and ensure softmax filters nulls. Patch in review: https://git.internal/redwood/repo/pull/987 (ops-only).

maya: follow-ups: - Confirm customer tests RC - Add telemetry to catch future string-score submissions (metric: rerank.score_parse_errors) - Add validation error code in response when we drop scores so customers see the issue instead of subtle ranking changes.

sam: CI fixed flaky tests, CI green now. Cutting RC tag: v1.4.3-rc.1. Jordan I'll DM the tarball and publish to npm as dist-tag `rc-1`.

jordan (customer): Got it, testing now. Quick note: while testing I hit a latency spike ~1.2s on a big request earlier today — not sure if related. I'll report if it's repeatable. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

maya: closing loop: once Jordan verifies I'll coordinate the full release and post a short support notice with mitigation steps (workaround: use direct curl until client updated; or sanitize candidate score types client-side).

ci-bot: @channel SDK release v1.4.3 published (rc -> stable) after QA.
